source.title: ExpertNet: Adversarial Learning and Recovery Against Noisy Labels
source.authors: Amirmasoud Ghiassi; R. Birke; Rui Han; L. Chen

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent cutoff or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how classification accuracy changes across synthetic label-noise ratios using a different, noise-aware architecture and validation accuracy measure.
record.gate_note: The paper varies symmetric label-noise ratios and reports validation accuracy. It does not report training error or test error at chance on completely random labels. Its comparison results concern ExpertNet and named competing methods; only results tied to the paper’s own noise-ratio evaluation are included.
record.test_reason: The study develops a mitigation for noisy labels and reports classification performance, without measuring memorization of corrupted labels. ExpertNet receives ground-truth labels during training and optionally noisy labels during inference. Its validation-accuracy trends do not test V4's joint claim of perfect training fit and degrading generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that ExpertNet improves classification robustness and data efficiency by combining images with noisy labels through mutually trained Amateur and Expert networks. This conclusion depends on access to ground-truth labels during training and, for full ExpertNet inference, noisy labels alongside images.
record.recipe_differences: ExpertNet uses an Amateur image classifier and an Expert network trained with both noisy and ground-truth labels; evaluation reports validation accuracy, not the original random-label fitting intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, symmetric noise ratio, and amount of training data vary; the paper also distinguishes Amateur-only from joint ExpertNet inference.

fits_no_version.finding: With all training data, ExpertNet validation accuracy declines from 89.23% to 80.73% on CIFAR-10 and from 86.72% to 66.11% on CIFAR-100 as corruption increases from 20% to 50%. Training uses ground-truth supervision; joint inference also receives noisy labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A classifier trained with ground-truth supervision can exploit noisy labels as auxiliary inputs to improve classification performance under label corruption.

record.problems: The reported metrics are validation accuracy rather than training error or test error; there is no completely random-label condition. The flattened tables make some method-to-value assignments difficult to recover, so no table-only values are extracted.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows retained. Tables 1–3 report accuracy for ExpertNet and competing methods, but those results do not measure the training-fit behavior required by V4; the prose likewise reports validation accuracy only.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random training labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect fitting of corrupted training labels while generalization degrades from clean labels through completely random labels. Only mitigation performance at 20–50% corruption is reported.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
The temporal order of learning shared patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's V4 designation from tested_not_extracted to not tested. Tables 1–3 are already declared in rows_left_out and require no missing-result entry. The introduction's AlexNet accuracy example is attributed to original source [30], not measured here. Qualitative statements about loss smoothness do not establish corrupted-label fitting or real-label-first learning.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling condition or training error is reported.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across true and random labels is reported.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are reported.
The study varies symmetric label-noise ratios and reports validation accuracy, but does not report whether training error remains perfect or how training fit changes.
Weight decay is part of the stated training setup, but the paper does not test whether regularization prevents fitting random labels or whether removing it harms generalization.
No learning-time analysis compares when real-label patterns versus noisy-label memorization are learned.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Uses memorization-informed noise-mitigation methods without testing random-label fitting, its timing, or the joint training-fit and generalization behavior in V4.

tranche.reason: Noise-mitigation study reporting inference accuracy; evaluated baselines exploit memorization, but no experiment measures the claim versions' training-fit behavior.

source_check.notes: ExpertNet requires ground-truth labels during training; full ExpertNet also uses noisy labels during inference. CIFAR noise rates are 20–50%; reported validation accuracy and qualitative loss convergence do not establish perfect fitting of corrupted labels.
